The forwarder representations filed in response to the Interim Report supported the proposed expansion of terminal areas, but assert that the proposal is the minimum expansion warranted by the evidence. The forwarders refer to the Court's decision in Freight ForwardersInstitute v. United States, supra, which remanded the Forwarder Terminal Areas, case supra, to this Commission for further proceedings considered with the Court's opinion, and suggest that the critical issue in the Forwarder Terminal Area case, supra, i.e., whether freight forwarder terminal areas should continue to be coterminous with commercial zone and motor carrier terminal area limits, be dealt with in a separate proceeding. They do not present additional evidence respecting the need for expansion of the existing freight forwarder terminal areas, but limit their representations to seeking amendment of the proposed regulations concerning the New York City-New Jersey suburb area. They point out that under the proposed rules, the population-mileage formula would apply to New York City and each municipality within the 20 mile area surrounding New York City, but carriers and forwarders serving such suburban municipalities would determine their terminal areas by reference to the population of the municipality in which they are located.
